function: Data-aided channel estimation: denoises detected symbols, selects the correct ones as extra pilots for LMMSE re-estimation; the same block also does direct symbol detection (p. 3).
system: Point-to-point MIMO-OFDM, 8x8 and 16x16 antennas, no RIS, 3.0 GHz carrier, 15 kHz subcarrier spacing, 256-point FFT (p. 12).
method: Variational-Bayes Denoising Block of three MLPs (prior, recognition, generative) trained supervised with a hybrid importance-weighted likelihood; SVM or MLP Correctness Classifier (p. 6).
data_channel: Generated 3GPP TDL-A/B/C channels at 3.0 GHz, 60K matrices (20K per model), 70% training, 15% validation, 15% test; no measured data (p. 12).
test_conditions: Trained and tested on the same TDL-A/B/C mix; tests sweep SNR -10 to 20 dB, 5-60 RBs, 8x8 and 16x16 antennas; tracking on TDL-A, 10 Hz (p. 14).
baselines: Classical: LS, LMMSE, MAP Data-Aided, DDCE, MAP Channel-Track, JCD (AMP). Learned: ChannelNet, CENet, Langevin diffusion (p. 12).
metrics: MSE of channel estimation, BER, classification accuracy of the Correctness Classifier, latency, and parameter count (p. 13).
complexity: Big-O complexity of each network (Eqs. 41-44) and Table 5 with parameters (~21K-42K) and latency (about 0.9-1.7 ms) (p. 14).
q1_support: p. 12: "follows the well-known 3GPP Tapped Delay Line models"
q2_support: p. 12: "70% utilized as the training set and the remaining data equally divided between the validation and test sets". Not met: no unseen scenario is tested; p. 16 says other antenna settings need retraining.
q3_support: p. 14: "surpasses conventional methods such as LS and LMMSE, DL-Based approaches such as CENet and ChannelNet"
q4_support: p. 14: "the computational complexities of our networks in DenoisingBlock are given by"
notes: Area 2 rather than 1: title and Section III present the data-aided channel estimator as the main contribution, judged by MSE and BER; direct symbol detection (p. 11) is a secondary mode. q1: the system model cites 3GPP TR 38.901 (ref 28, p. 4 and p. 18), while the Doppler values cite TR 36.913. q2: the RB sweep (5-60) equals the Table 3 data range and p. 12 says training covers diverse RB scenarios, so it is counted as in-distribution; reviewer may check. Table 5 (16x16 setting, p. 14) lists latencies of 0.92-1.71 ms for the proposed variants, while the text gives 0.6-0.8 ms without naming the configuration (p. 15).
